## Bristol Instagram and Facebook caption

<!-- bristol-caption-start -->
Bristol, what shall we do this weekend? Four ideas for 19–20 September 👇

🎶 SING ALONG — Sea Shanty Shout, Great Eastern Hall, Brunel Square. Sat + Sun noon–6pm. Free, no booking; donations welcome. This is in the hall, not aboard the SS Great Britain.

⛵ MAKE & EXPLORE — Docks Heritage Weekend at M Shed. Sat + Sun, with children's paper-boat making on Saturday. Museum open 10am–5pm, entry free; crane visits and boat trips cost extra. Workshop times, cost and booking aren't separately listed—check with the museum before making a special trip.

🥁 MUSIC & NATURE — Trinity Community Celebration, Sunday noon–4pm. Nature/craft drop-ins, live music and youth performances. £0–£3 donation; all ages, under-14s with an adult. Check with Trinity about individual workshops and access needs. Parking is charged.

🌿 ROOM TO ROAM — Tyntesfield's final free-entry weekend. Sat + Sun, estate 10am–6pm, last entry 5pm; no booking. Non-member parking £5. Expect slopes/gravel; pushchairs can't go inside the house.

Going with little ones? Pick a short visit and let them set the pace. Great Eastern Hall and M Shed give you indoor options; dockside cobbles need care with wheels.

Save this for Saturday. DoNext Bristol: https://donext.co.uk/bristol/

## Cardiff Instagram and Facebook caption — prepared, blocked

Cardiff weekend plans for 19–20 September: one Open Doors find and three easy-to-fit-in regular visits.

🔎 St Margaret's Church, Roath: children's quiz, free, no booking. Saturday 12:30–5:30pm or Sunday 2–5:30pm. Church visit only for our family pick—the tower is adults-only.

🏛️ National Museum Cardiff: free general entry, 10am–5pm both days; galleries close 4:45pm. An indoor option for a short browse together. Under 16s with an adult; some exhibitions cost extra.

🌳 Bute Park sculpture trail: spot the carvings and try the climbable frog, beetle and hollow log. Free outdoor exploring; choose your own short route and dress for the weather.

🕰️ St Fagans: explore historic buildings and bring a picnic. Daily 10am–5pm, entry free, parking £7. Under 16s with an adult; uneven paths and restricted pushchair access inside historic buildings. Extras may cost.

Details: https://cadw.gov.wales/open-doors-st-margarets-church-roath
https://museum.wales/cardiff/visit/
https://bute-park.com/attraction/sculpture-trail/
https://museum.wales/stfagans/visit/

Save a plan for your family: https://donext.co.uk/
Checked 18 September; check venue updates before setting off.

## Birmingham Instagram and Facebook caption — prepared, blocked

Birmingham, here are four family finds for 19–20 September—all with free entry.

🚍 SATURDAY: Brum Transport Festival, 11am–5pm. Explore vehicles across Victoria, Centenary and Hippodrome squares. No booking.

🎺 SUNDAY: Moor Pool Heritage Festival, 11am–3pm. Crafts, trails, LEGO and sports tasters around Moor Pool Hall and the estate. No booking; some paths are uneven and there are steps. Hall wheelchair access is at the side.

✂️ SUNDAY: Make a Mini Museum at Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery, 11am–3pm. Free Marvellous Makers drop-in for all ages, with adult supervision.

🦖 EITHER DAY: Lapworth Museum, noon–5pm. Fossils, minerals and Roary the dinosaur indoors. Free, no booking; wheelchair/pram access and babychange. Weekend campus parking £3.

Details: https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/brum-transport-festival/
https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/moor-pool-heritage-festival/
https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/events/marvellous-makers
https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/cultural-attractions/lapworth-museum-of-geology/visit-us

Which would your child choose? https://donext.co.uk/birmingham/

## Bristol Friday weekend email — draft only

Subject: Bristol: sing, make and roam this weekend

Hi there,

For 19–20 September, try free Sea Shanty Shout concerts at Great Eastern Hall, noon–6pm both days, or M Shed's Docks Heritage Weekend: paper boats on Saturday and harbour demonstrations across the weekend. Museum entry is free; boats/cranes are charged, and workshop details need checking.

On Sunday, Trinity has music and nature/craft drop-ins, noon–4pm, for a £0–£3 donation. Tyntesfield's free-entry offer ends Sunday; estate 10am–6pm, last entry 5pm, parking £5.

## Bristol weekday email — 21–25 September, draft only

Subject: Bristol: a little making, a little music

Hi there,

Need a small outing next week? Arnolfini's free Arnold Art Cart is available Tuesday–Friday 11am–6pm on the second floor, with creative materials for families.

For younger children, Central Library's regular timetable lists Monday and Wednesday rhyme sessions at 10:45am for 0–3s, and Friday storytime at 10:45am for 1–4s. Free, no booking; older siblings welcome. These are recurring sessions, so check the timetable before travelling.

[Art Cart](https://arnolfini.org.uk/whatson/arnold-art-cart/) · [Library timetable](https://www.bristol.gov.uk/residents/libraries-and-archives/services-for-children-and-young-people/baby-bounce-and-rhyme-and-storytime-sessions)
